episodes.title: Robert Friedland on the World's Monumental Shortage of Copper
episodes.summary:
**Summary**
Robert Friedland (Ivanhoe Mines) argues copper is now "the new oil" — a structurally undersupplied critical metal at the center of energy transition, AI/data-center buildout, and great-power competition. Copper hit a record ~$14,875/ton this week (down ~3% into the taping) as B of A flagged the first annual output decline since 2017, even as demand for grid, EV, defense and AI infrastructure accelerates.

**Key points**
- Ore grades are collapsing (Chile's Escondida down from 2% to 0.8%, heading to 0.4% in two years), forcing more energy/water-intensive processing even as output falls.
- Global sulfuric acid (needed to leach ~25% of copper supply) spiked from $150/ton to over $1,000/ton after Strait of Hormuz-linked gas disruptions and Russia/China export bans — an under-the-radar inflation channel.
- Mining capex has been starved for decades (NPV models undervalue long-life mines); mining is now <1% of S&P 500 market cap, while China has systematically bought up the global critical-minerals supply chain.
- White House undecided on refined copper tariffs (Reuters story pressuring copper price on Sep 10); Friedland notes a 30% tariff would push US copper to ~$7.87/lb, aiding reindustrialization but adding to domestic inflation ahead of midterms.
- US-China tension over critical metals (gallium, scandium, rhenium, niobium) is becoming a chokepoint akin to a Boeing engines-for-China-metals standoff described via Treasury Secretary Bessent.

**FX / rates implications**
- Persistent yen weakness (cited 160/USD) makes copper/commodity imports far more expensive for Japan, reinforcing BoJ policy tension and carry-trade dynamics (Bessent reportedly wary of a JPY collapse curbing Japanese UST demand, which would push US yields higher).
- Diesel/refined-product price spikes (crack spreads at all-time highs) and Hormuz-related disruption are a stagflationary commodity impulse relevant to broad EM inflation/rates pricing.
- Tariff uncertainty on refined copper is a two-sided US inflation/growth risk factor markets are actively pricing.

**Watch list**
- White House decision on refined copper tariffs.
- Copper price action following the Reuters tariff report (recorded Sep 10, down ~3% on the week).
- USD/JPY levels and any BoJ/MOF intervention risk tied to carry-trade unwind and Treasury demand.
- Sulfuric acid supply and Russia/China export bans as a hidden inflation channel.

episodes.title: Cut to the Chase! Fed outlook after the latest US inflation report
episodes.summary:
**Summary**
Standard Chartered now sees a 90% probability the Fed hikes rates at its September 15-16 FOMC meeting, a sharp jump in conviction driven by a stronger-than-expected August jobs report and a hotter core CPI print. This matters for EM traders because a hawkish surprise from the world's most important central bank drives the USD, UST yields, and global risk appetite that EM Asia and LATAM currencies trade off.

**Key points**
- August payrolls added 162,000 jobs, nearly triple consensus, with prior two months revised up; unemployment held at 4.1%.
- Core CPI rose 0.3% m/m vs 0.2% expected; headline inflation 3.4% y/y, with gasoline (+3.9% m/m) driving over a third of the move.
- Fed voted 9-3 to hold in July; Governor Waller signaled his vote hinges on this inflation data, tipping the balance toward a hike.
- Chair Warsh has called the current 3.75% policy rate "not restrictive"; political pressure from President Trump for cuts raises independence concerns if the Fed holds.
- StanChart's base case is one "credibility hike," not a new tightening cycle — annual core inflation still easing (2.4% from 2.5%), wage growth at a 5-year low (3.1% y/y).
- Key risk: "super core" services-ex-housing inflation jumped 0.5% m/m (strongest since January, 3% y/y), suggesting price pressures could broaden if WTI holds above $100/bbl.

**FX / rates implications**
- A Fed hike plus hawkish messaging would lift the USD broadly and pressure EM Asia/LATAM FX (INR, IDR, PHP, MXN, BRL) via higher UST yields, with 10-year potentially testing the 2023 high of 5.02%.
- A dovish-leaning press conference despite the hike could cap USD upside and ease pressure on carry trades.
- StanChart extended bond duration to 3-7 years on the yield rise but avoids ultra-long maturities given fiscal deficit risks.

**Watch list**
- FOMC decision and press conference, September 16 — is it "one and done" or a tightening bias.
- US 10-year yield vs. the 2023 high of 5.02%.
- WTI crude relative to $100/bbl as a pass-through risk to services inflation.
